category_title: Verbal students with autism who discuss negative topics and use headsets to avoid interaction
minimal_context: Jordan is walking through the hallway between classes and practicing using his communication book to talk to a classmate.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jordan, it is time to transition to your next class. Let's use your communication book to talk to a classmate in the hallway.

STUDENT: (Walks rapidly through the hallway listening to music on a headset, rarely smiling.)

TUTOR: Please take off your headset and try to start a conversation.

STUDENT: (Takes off the headset and greets a peer) Hi. I got poor grades.

TUTOR: What else can you say to them?

STUDENT: (Appears angry) My family has problems. I’m gonna Taser that kid . . .

options.A: Prior to hallway interactions, explain to peers that Jordan is learning to converse. Show them the communication book, instruct them to respond naturally, and encourage them to ask reciprocal questions.
options.B: Apply increasingly serious disciplinary measures if the disturbing comments continue during hallway transitions, utilizing consequences such as classroom suspension, detention, and school suspension.
options.C: Observe the occurrences of the disturbing comments during hallway transitions all day, recording the behavioral data in scatter plots and ABC charts when the school day finishes.
options.D: Adhere to a strict transition routine and provide positive reinforcement for desired conversational behaviors in the hallway, utilizing rewards such as social praise or stickers on a chart.
